questions.text: Can you tell me a little about your hometown?
questions.say: Good morning. My name is Lily, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about your hometown. Can you tell me a little about your hometown?

questions.text: Are there any parks or green spaces there?
questions.say: Are there any parks or green spaces there?

questions.text: Would you like to work in your hometown one day?
questions.say: Would you like to work in your hometown one day?

questions.text: How has your hometown changed since you were a child?
questions.say: How has your hometown changed since you were a child?

questions.text: Do you mind waiting in queues?
questions.say: Now let's move on to talk about queues. Do you mind waiting in queues?

questions.text: Where do you often have to queue?
questions.say: Where do you often have to queue?

questions.text: Do people in your country queue patiently?

questions.text: What can you see from your bedroom window?
questions.say: What can you see from your bedroom window?

questions.text: Do you prefer rooms with a lot of natural light?

cueCard.topic: Describe a time when you forgot something important.
cueCard.explain: and explain how you felt when you realised you had forgotten it.

questions.text: Describe a time when you forgot something important.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a time when you forgot something important. You should say: what you forgot; when it happened; what you did about it; and explain how you felt when you realised you had forgotten it.

questions.text: What do you do now to help yourself remember things?
questions.say: Thank you. What do you do now to help yourself remember things?

questions.text: Why do some people have a better memory than others?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a time when you forgot something important, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all memory. Why do some people have a better memory than others?

questions.text: What kinds of things are easy to remember, and what kinds are difficult?
questions.say: What kinds of things are easy to remember, and what kinds are difficult?

questions.text: Do older people remember things differently from young people?
questions.say: Do older people remember things differently from young people?

questions.text: Do people remember less now that they can find everything on their phones?
questions.say: Now let's talk about remembering and technology. Do people remember less now that they can find everything on their phones?

questions.text: Should students still have to learn things by heart at school?
questions.say: Should students still have to learn things by heart at school?

questions.text: Is it a problem that so many personal memories are kept only as digital photos?
questions.say: Is it a problem that so many personal memories are kept only as digital photos?
